base_rationale: CAM is the more complete and legible witness in this chapter: it has 0 illegible tokens versus GG's 1 deliberate scribal erasure (GG v.5), and a lower uncertainty rate (32/317 = 10.1%% of CAM tokens flagged vs 40/316 = 12.7%% in GG). CAM's parchment is clean with no staining over the chapter-3 text, whereas GG carries multiple red inline reading-glosses and split/faded clusters. CAM was transcribed directly from the hi-res Cambridge UL MS Add. 1570 images (no low-resolution pass for this chapter), and the project GAPS source-map designates Cambridge the primary Samuel witness; this chapter's own completeness and uncertainty numbers independently confirm that choice.

verses.semantic_note: 3:1 = the child Samuel ministered to the LORD before Eli; word of the LORD rare, no open vision in those days. Both witnesses carry exactly this (GG/CAM differ only ቃሉ/ነገረ for 'word').
3:2 = Eli lying in his place, eyes beginning to grow dim so he could not see. Matches; CAM keeps 'could not see' here, GG carries it into v3 (segmentation variant, noted).
3:3 = lamp of God not yet gone out; Samuel sleeping in the temple where the ark of God was. Matches; GG opens with the 'could not see' clause CAM placed in v2 (verse-fusion variant).
3:4 = the LORD called Samuel; he answered 'Here am I'. Matches; CAM folds 'and he said, Here am I' into v4, GG carries it at the head of v5 (segmentation variant).
3:5 = Samuel ran to Eli 'thou calledst me'; Eli 'I called not; lie down again'. Matches; GG has the scribal-erasure lacuna here (one illegible token).
3:6 = the LORD called again; Samuel rose, went to Eli; Eli 'I called not, my son; lie down'. Matches (GG carries a red inline reading-gloss 'to him: whom'; CAM adds 'my son').
3:7 = Samuel did not yet know the LORD, neither was the word yet revealed to him. Matches (GG prefixes a recension repetition of v6's close).
3:8 = the LORD called Samuel the third time; he went to Eli; Eli perceived the LORD had called the child. Matches closely (near 1:1).
3:9 = Eli told Samuel: lie down, and if called say 'Speak, LORD, for thy servant heareth'. Matches (CAM expands with 'and tell me').
3:10 = the LORD came, stood, called as before; Samuel: 'Speak, for thy servant heareth' (the project's anchored v.10 note). Matches closely.
3:11 = the LORD will do a thing in Israel at which both ears of every hearer shall tingle (1sa.py topic CONNIVANCE/WICKED at 3:11). Matches.
3:12 = in that day I will perform against Eli all I have spoken concerning his house. Matches (second half phrased differently between recensions).
3:13 = I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity he knew, his sons made themselves vile and he restrained them not (1sa.py topic CHILDREN at 3:13). Matches.
3:14 = therefore I have sworn the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever (1sa.py topic UNPARDONABLE SIN at 3:14). Matches.
3:15 = Samuel lay until morning, opened the doors of the house of the LORD, and feared to tell Eli the vision. Matches (GG adds 'and awoke in the morning').
3:16 = Eli called Samuel 'my son'; Samuel answered 'Here am I'. Matches (near 1:1).
3:17 = Eli: what was said? hide it not; God do so to thee if thou hide anything. Matches (heavy orthographic divergence, same content).
3:18 = Samuel told him every whit, hid nothing; Eli said 'It is the LORD; let him do what seemeth good'. Matches.
3:19 = Samuel grew, the LORD was with him and let none of his words fall to the ground. Matches (CAM has a ቃሉ dittography + word-order shift).
3:20 = all Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew Samuel was established a prophet of the LORD. Matches.

3:21 = the LORD appeared again in Shiloh, revealed himself by the word of the LORD; the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Both match this core; GG carries an additional LXX-style expansion ('from end to end of the land... and Samuel grew, but they walked in evil ways before the LORD') -- a recension plus, not a contradiction, so semantic_pass holds.

metrics.lacuna_counts_note: lacuna_counts.gg (1) == the count of ⟦illegible⟧ tokens in 1sa3_witnessGG.json (one deliberate scribal erasure, v.5 token_index 3); lacuna_counts.cam (0) == the count of ⟦illegible⟧ tokens in 1sa3_witnessCAM_hires.json (CAM transcription_notes: 'No glyph was wholly illegible (0 illegible tokens)'); lacuna_counts.both (0) = positions illegible in BOTH witnesses. Per-verse lacuna breakdown: v5 gg=1 cam=0 both=0. All 1 lacuna-* row(s) are EXCLUDED from every agreement denominator (strict, skeleton, both-confident). Genuine textual plus/minus (a token present in one witness, absent-but-legible in the other) is represented with an empty string on the absent side and class 'disagree' and IS counted in the aligned denominator -- it is real divergence, not a lacuna. CAM was transcribed directly from hi-res images; there was no low-resolution pass for this chapter, so no delta_vs_lowres block is reported.

definitions.strict: exact literal token-string identity / (agree+disagree) aligned pairs
definitions.skeleton: diacritic/order-folded + near-homograph-folded token equality (class==agree) / (agree+disagree) aligned pairs, full aligned denominator. Fold tolerance: Ge'ez vowel-order folded to syllable-block consonant base; near-homograph fidels folded (ሰ/ሠ, ሐ/ኀ/ኃ/ነ, አ/ዐ, ጸ/ፀ) plus this recension's documented s/l swap (ስ↔ለ, e.g. GG ስእግዚአብᙔር for CAM ለእግዚአብᙔር) and CAM's habitual ሾሉ for ኵሉ.
definitions.both_confident: skeleton-equal / aligned pairs where neither witness flagged that token uncertain or illegible (gap/insertion cells and lacuna rows also excluded from this denominator)
